title: Bounded-flat coefficient/site square with its canonical derived comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, and let $a\le b$ be integers. Use ordinary constant-ring module categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For $R=A,B$, write $N_R=\nu_X^*$ for the exact constant-coefficient module inverse image [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], also applied termwise and on derived categories. Let $P$ be a cochain complex of etale $A_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Put $P_B=P\otimes_{A_X}B_X$ and $(N_AP)_B=(N_AP)\otimes_{A_X}B_X$, with the target-ring action on the second factor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension]. Write $Q$ for the appropriate derived localization.
The complexes $P$, $P_B$, $N_AP$, $(N_AP)_B$ and $N_B(P_B)$ have flat terms, are zero outside $[a,b]$, and are K-flat against arbitrary acyclic complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There are natural derived-category isomorphisms $Q(P_B)\simeq Q(P)\otimes_A^L B$, $Q(N_AP)\simeq N_AQ(P)$ and $Q((N_AP)_B)\simeq (N_AQ(P))\otimes_A^L B$. The canonical termwise tensor comparison gives a $B_X$-linear isomorphism of complexes $N_B(P_B)\xrightarrow{\sim}(N_AP)_B$, natural in chain maps of $P$. The scalar representative arrows are the adjunction transposes of the localized ordinary scalar units [def-sp-coefficient-scalar-representatives]. Under the displayed representative identifications, its derived image is the inverse of the canonical scalar-adjunction mate of the exact restriction/site square, namely the comparison of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility]. Each of the five localized complexes has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on its own ringed site, meaning that its derived tensor with every module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology zero outside this interval [def-kun-tor-amplitude, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. No constructibility of $P$, Noetherianity of $X$, or flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] for both $A$ and $B$. It identifies inverse images of the constant ring sheaves with the corresponding constant ring sheaves on the pro-etale site, and makes $N_A,N_B$ exact module inverse images. These identifications respect $A\to B$, since the inverse image of a constant-sheaf ring map is the same map on constant values. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], termwise $N_R$ represents its derived functor, naturally in complexes; in particular $Q(N_AP)\simeq N_AQ(P)$.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), exact inverse-image case; sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact)

proof.text: View extension $A_X\to B_X$ on either site as the module pullback for the identity geometric morphism with this coefficient map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] first to $P^q$ for the etale coefficient extension, then for $N_A$ and $N_B$, and finally for the pro-etale coefficient extension. It gives flat terms in $P_B,N_AP,N_B(P_B),(N_AP)_B$, over their respective target rings. These functors send zero modules to zero: inverse image is additive, and $0\otimes B_X=0$ by the definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus all five complexes are zero outside $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 05VD (lemma-pullback-flat), applied to constant coefficients and identity geometric morphisms

proof.text: Each complex of Step 2 is bounded above by $b$ and has flat terms on its own ringed site. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] separately to the five complexes. This proves K-flatness against every acyclic complex, without a boundedness condition on that test complex. The sites are taken on small representatives in an ambient module universe, as in the site's definitions, so the lemma's relative size hypothesis holds for both sites.

Apply the computation isomorphism $\epsilon_P$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to the identity geometric morphism with coefficient map $A_X\to B_X$ on the etale site, and apply it to $N_AP$ on the pro-etale site. Step 3 verifies its K-flat flat-term hypotheses. The derived functors are precisely the derived scalar extensions of [def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension]; invert the computation maps to obtain $Q(P_B)\simeq Q(P)\otimes_A^L B$ and $Q((N_AP)_B)\simeq(N_AQ(P))\otimes_A^L B$, using Step 1 for the latter. Naturality in chain maps is the naturality of $\epsilon$ and of the exact-functor localization identification.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), computation on K-flat complexes with flat terms

proof.text: Specialize the ordinary comparison $\chi_h$ in [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] to $h=\nu_X$ and $A_X\to B_X$. Step 1 supplies its inverse-image coefficient identifications. Interchanging the two tensor factors translates its left-factor convention to the right-factor convention here: both interchanges are $b\otimes p\mapsto p\otimes b$, which are inverse balanced maps by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This gives in degree $q$ the $B_X$-linear isomorphism $\chi^q:N_B(P^q\otimes_A B)\to N_A(P^q)\otimes_A B$. Naturality with respect to $d_P^q$ says $\chi^{q+1}N_B(d_P^q\otimes1)=(N_A(d_P^q)\otimes1)\chi^q$, so these components form an isomorphism of complexes. The same naturality equation for each component of a chain map proves the required naturality in $P$.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); balanced comparison and its naturality

proof.text: The derived normalization clause of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] identifies the inverse of this localized chain comparison, with the identifications in Steps 1 and 4, with the canonical scalar-adjunction mate; hence $Q(\chi)$ has the required direction. To check its identification with the tensor-pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $V\to B_X[0]$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. On $(P,V)$ the latter comparison is the localization of the ordinary total tensor comparison (Tag 07A4). By [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization], tensoring $V\to B_X[0]$ with $P$ or with $N_AP$ gives the canonical computation isomorphisms. Exactness of $N_A$ also preserves that quasi-isomorphism. The ordinary tensor comparison is natural in its second factor, so its square for $V\to B_X[0]$ commutes. Inverting the vertical computation maps therefore identifies its bottom map with $Q(\chi)$. The $B_X$ action in this square is the action on the coefficient factor; its compatibility is precisely the $B_X$-linear scalar normalization already supplied by $\chi_h$. Thus this is equality with the canonical derived scalar/site map, including the target-ring action, rather than just an isomorphism between its source and target.

Let $C$ be any one of the five complexes, and let $M$ be any module sheaf over its own coefficient ring on its own site, in degree zero. Steps 2 and 3 put $C$ in the flat-term K-flat class. By [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization], $QC\otimes^L M$ is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes M[0])$. Its degree $q$ term is $C^q\otimes M$, and its differential is $d_C^q\otimes1$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For $q\notin[a,b]$ this term is zero; its cohomology is then zero since its kernel and image in that degree are both zero. This proves the universal Tor test in [def-kun-tor-amplitude] or [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], respectively. The argument uses flatness of the terms over their target rings, not flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$. It uses neither constructibility nor Noetherianity.

It adds 7 proof steps to the statement-only item that Q18 created on 2026-10-22; there are no new nodes and no repair or re-split note. I tested the statement on Z/4→F_2 with P=A[0] and with (A--2-->A), and on the trivial cases P=0, a=b, B=0 and A=B. It holds and is what the parent lem-sp-finite-coefficient-input-models needs in its Step 2. Step checks: (1) lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact clauses 1-2 together with exact-functor-derived-factorization give Q(N_AP)≅N_AQ(P). (2) ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback allows an arbitrary ring map, giving flat terms over the target ring; the support stays in [a,b]. (3) independent-bounded-flat-kflat is Stacks 06YQ and gives K-flatness against every acyclic complex. (4) ringed-topoi-derived-pullback ε on flat-term K-flat P gives the scalar-extension representatives; the B⊗P versus P⊗B swap is trivial. (5) The χ_h of sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization specialized to ν is B-linear and natural (Stacks 03EL), so the components form a chain isomorphism. (6) Q(χ)^{-1}=θ, and it agrees with the tensor-pullback comparison through a K-flat resolution V→B[0], the one-sided normalization and naturality (Stacks 07A4). I accept reading 'canonical' as the representative comparison, which parent and other citers also use. (7) Tot(C⊗M[0]) has terms C^q⊗M, which vanish outside [a,b] (Stacks 08G1, (2)⇒(1), checked at line 12432). All Stacks tags exist with the stated labels, and nothing cites SGA. No duplicates: lem-sp-etale-open-counit-flat-models is an open-immersion counit special case. I accept the 8 declared tool_uses as generic black boxes. Batch-5: the flagged node lem-pod-derived-exact-square-composition is a formal pasting statement for exact functors (Stacks 05S7/014F) and not a step of Poincaré duality. Recomputing the batch-5 closure with and without the new item→sfb-kflat edge gives the same 20282 nodes: both nodes are already reached through other citers, so the citation adds nothing. Accepted. No changes.
